record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.context_brief: one-way functions from CL to NC0
record.original_question: Can one prove that if one-way functions exist in catalytic logspace CL, or even if some one-way function is computable by a polynomial-size polynomial-length register program, then one-way functions already exist in NC0?

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Prove that the existence of one-way functions in CL, or even any one-way function computable by a poly-size poly-length register program, implies the existence of one-way functions in NC0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) A function f : {0,1}* -> {0,1}* is called a one-way function if it is computable in polynomial time and, for every probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm A, every polynomial p, and all sufficiently large n,
    Pr_{x ~ {0,1}^n}[ A(1^n, f(x)) ∈ f^{-1}(f(x)) ] < 1/p(n).

(2) NC^0 denotes the class of functions f : {0,1}* -> {0,1}* computable by a uniform family of constant-depth, bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits; equivalently, each output bit of f depends on only O(1) input bits.

(3) Catalytic logspace, denoted CL, is the class of languages (or functions) decidable (computable) by a Turing machine equipped with a read-only input tape, an O(log n)-size read/write clean work tape, and an additional polynomially long "catalytic" auxiliary tape that may be initialized with arbitrary content, may be read and written during the computation, but must be restored to its initial contents at the end of the computation, for every input and every initial content of the auxiliary tape.

(4) A register program of length L over R registers, each holding an element of a finite group (or ring) of size 2^O(1), is a sequence of L instructions of the form r_i <- r_i · g(x), r_i <- r_i + g(x_{j_1}, ..., x_{j_k}), or similar bounded local updates depending on a constant number of input bits, where the output is read off from designated registers at the end. The program has poly-size if R is polynomial in n, and poly-length if L is polynomial in n.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following implication: if there exists a one-way function computable in catalytic logspace CL — or, more generally, if there exists a one-way function computable by a polynomial-size, polynomial-length register program in the sense above — then there exists a one-way function in NC^0.
artifact.status_search_result: This is listed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on catalytic/reusable-space computation, posed alongside related questions about basing cryptographic primitives in NC^0 on assumptions in catalytic logspace. No solution or partial result resolving the implication "OWF in CL (or in poly-size poly-length register programs) ⇒ OWF in NC^0" appears in the literature retrieved.
